title: Petra and the Inventory
premise: Casper Reyes, once the conservatory's most celebrated piano prodigy, returns twenty years later not to play but to clean its halls before the building is sold. When she discovers a box of undelivered letters hidden behind a wardrobe in her old practice room — letters written by her late teacher, Marta Ilves, to a student who vanished mid-career — Casper realizes she was meant to receive them and never did. As demolition looms, she tracks down the letters' intended recipient, confronts the silence that ended her own career, and gathers an unlikely found family of former students and staff to give the conservatory a proper farewell. In the end, Casper reads the final letter aloud in the empty concert hall on the last night before the sale closes, says goodbye out loud at last, and chooses to stay in the city — not as a prodigy or a janitor, but as the keeper of what remains.
about_author: Elodie Crane is the pen name of a writer who spent a decade working night shifts in institutional buildings and swears the corridors talk after midnight. She lives near a decommissioned music school and writes about the people who stay behind when institutions end.

chapters.title: The Keys She Still Carries
chapters.summary: Casper Reyes clocks in for her first shift as a janitor at the conservatory where she was once a prodigy, now slated for sale. POV: Casper. The beat is quiet dread — she knows every hallway by muscle memory and hates that she does.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Casper's ritual: she catalogs everything she can't say in a pocket notebook — apologies, explanations, one sentence to Marta Ilves, her dead teacher. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: the comfort and prison of silence.

chapters.title: Night Shift Choir
chapters.summary: Casper meets the skeleton crew: Dev, a chatty security guard; Ruthie, the archivist refusing to pack; and Tomas, a teenage work-study kid who doesn't know who she was. POV: Casper. Beat: reluctant warmth, the first threads of found family.

chapters.title: Room 214
chapters.summary: Assigned to clear her old practice room, Casper finds a wardrobe bolted to the wall — and behind it, a tin box of letters, all addressed in Marta's hand to 'C.R.' and never sent. POV: Casper. Beat: vertigo; the past physically dislodged.

chapters.title: What Marta Wrote
chapters.summary: Casper reads the first three letters: Marta writing to a student who disappeared before a career-defining recital, full of tenderness and guilt. POV: Casper with flashbacks to Marta. Beat: grief reopening like a door she'd nailed shut.

chapters.title: Ruthie Knows Something
chapters.summary: Casper shows Ruthie one letter; Ruthie goes pale and admits Marta asked her to hide the box decades ago, calling it 'a debt unpaid.' POV: alternating Casper/Ruthie. Beat: complicity across generations of silence.

chapters.title: The Student Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Digging through archives, Casper learns the letters were addressed to Lena Okafor, a violinist who left mid-year in 1999 and never came back. POV: Casper. Beat: obsession kindling — someone else's unfinished goodbye mirrors her own.

chapters.title: Dev's Theory
chapters.summary: Over vending-machine coffee, Dev — who reads people for a living — gently names what Casper won't: she didn't come back for a paycheck. POV: Casper. Beat: being seen against her will; resistance softening.

chapters.title: Recital, Interrupted (Flashback)
chapters.summary: A full flashback chapter: seventeen-year-old Casper freezes mid-performance, walks offstage, and Marta says nothing — the silence that ended everything. POV: young Casper. Beat: the wound shown, not told.

chapters.title: Finding Lena
chapters.summary: Tomas's internet sleuthing turns up Lena Okafor running a repair shop two states away, fixing violins instead of playing them. POV: Casper/Tomas. Beat: hope with teeth; the clock ticking toward the sale date.

chapters.title: The Road Trip Nobody Approved
chapters.summary: Casper, Dev, and Tomas drive to meet Lena, who initially slams the door — then sees Marta's handwriting and lets them in. POV: Casper. Beat: love against duty; strangers becoming allies over shared loss.

chapters.title: Lena's Side of It
chapters.summary: Lena reveals why she left: Marta pushed her toward a career she didn't want, and the letters arrived too late to matter — or so Lena believed. POV: Lena. Beat: anger and tenderness entangled; duty dressed as love.

chapters.title: The Letter That Changes Everything
chapters.summary: Among the letters they find one addressed not to Lena but to Casper herself — dated the week after her failed recital, saying Marta's silence wasn't disappointment but fear. POV: Casper. Beat: devastation and release colliding.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Sale
chapters.summary: Back home, the buyers move up the closing date; Ruthie discovers records are being shredded early. The crew decides to fight for one last night in the hall. POV: rotating cast. Beat: stakes sharpen from personal to collective.

chapters.title: Petitions and Piano Wire
chapters.summary: The crew petitions, schemes, and fails through official channels — until Tomas suggests asking the buyers directly, person to person. POV: Casper. Beat: humility as strategy; asking instead of hiding.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Daughter
chapters.summary: The buyer's adult daughter, a lapsed cellist, visits the hall and hears Casper play for the first time in twenty years — badly, then honestly. POV: Casper/daughter. Beat: music as confession; an unexpected advocate.

chapters.title: One Night, Granted
chapters.summary: The buyer agrees: one final evening, no press, no audience beyond whoever shows. Word spreads anyway. POV: Casper. Beat: terror and gratitude; the impossible made conditional.

chapters.title: Setting the Stage
chapters.summary: Preparations: Ruthie unpacks the archive, Lena arrives with her repaired violin, chairs are set out for ghosts and strangers alike. POV: rotating cast. Beat: found family assembling in earnest.

chapters.title: The Last Concert
chapters.summary: The farewell concert: Lena plays, students perform, and Casper takes the stage last, playing the piece she fled from — finishing it this time. POV: Casper. Beat: catharsis; the body finally doing what the heart demanded.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Alone-ish in the emptied hall, Casper reads Marta's final letter aloud, then speaks her own inventory into the room — every unsaid thing, said. POV: Casper. Beat: the climax of voice; goodbye performed properly at last.

chapters.title: Closing Day
chapters.summary: The sale closes; keys are handed over; the crew scatters but exchanges numbers, addresses, promises. Casper gives Tomas her old practice-room key as a keepsake. POV: Casper. Beat: bittersweet severance; endings held gently.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Months later, Casper teaches free Saturday lessons in a borrowed church basement — Lena, Dev, Ruthie, and Tomas orbiting close. The inventory notebook now holds only things worth keeping. POV: Casper. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; a quiet, earned resolution.
